pr.title: Pass project ios's bundle ID to AppleScript as an argument, and test Ctrl-C in logs
pr.head: 0bd241e838dbc5d87f767622e3cd749019463884

summary: project ios builds a branch of a repository's iOS app and puts it on a device or, with --mac, opens it on this Mac. This pull request takes four small follow-ups that the reviews of the original project ios stack left open, now that the stack is merged.

• The bundle ID never becomes AppleScript source. On a Mac, the command asks osascript whether the app is running and tells it to quit before opening a new build. The app's bundle ID, which comes from the project's build settings, used to be pasted into the script text, so a quote in it could change the script. Both calls now go through one helper that passes the ID as an argument.
  • Ctrl-C during logs is tested. logs already removed its half-written file and the device's log archive on any exception, Ctrl-C included. A new test proves it, so narrowing that handler would now fail the suite.
  • Three long Markdown lines are rewrapped, one in docs/cli.md and two in the ios plan, with no words changed.
  • The ios plan's outcome records the iPhone check. The last acceptance criterion, a real install on an iPhone, ran after the merge and passed.
The review found the code and tests right. It flagged one thing: the ios plan is already completed, and the repository says to leave a completed plan as it is.

groups.title: The bundle ID reaches AppleScript as an argument
groups.kicker: One helper builds both osascript calls, and a test proves the ID never enters the script.
intro: Every build of an app shares one bundle ID, the reverse-DNS name such as com.example.myapp that macOS uses to find the app. Before project ios --mac opens a new build, it checks whether a copy with that ID is running, and quits it, through osascript, the command that runs AppleScript.

The new helper app_script wraps a statement in on run argv … end run and puts the bundle ID after the script as its argument. The statement reads it as item 1 of argv, so the ID is data to AppleScript whatever characters it holds.

files.note: Adds app_script and routes the running check and the quit through it.

checks.text: Ran the real osascript with this script form: it returns true for com.apple.finder. A bundle ID holding a quote, a backslash, and a do shell script clause comes back as an unknown-application error, so nothing it holds runs. Nothing was quit or launched.
The quit script compiles with osacompile, and open_on_mac is the only caller of running and app_script.

files.note: The stand-in osascript finds the running check in any argument now, and two tests are new: a bundle ID with a quote, and Ctrl-C during the log collect.

checks.text: Splicing the bundle ID back into the running script on a copy of the head turns this test red.
Narrowing logs's except BaseException to except Exception turns this test red, and so does moving the archive removal out of its finally.

groups.title: Rewrapped lines and the plan's outcome
groups.kicker: Formatting in the CLI reference and the plan, and a new ending for the plan's outcome.
intro: The rewrapped lines change no words, which the review checked word by word. The plan's § 8 Outcome also changes: it said the person would run the iPhone check after the merge, and it now says they ran it, that the check was tracked in their Projector inbox, and that it passed.

files.note: Rewraps the paragraph on which commands take --json.
Rewraps two lines and rewrites § 8 Outcome to record the iPhone check's result.

checks.text: The ios plan was already completed on main. The repository's projects README, under “Leave a completed plan as it is”, allows a completed plan to change only through the project commands and rename updates. The review asks to revert this file and record the check's result in the pull request body instead.
